In a sense, the processes of integra- tion and differentiation are “inverses” of each other. The Fundamental Theorem also says that every continuous function ƒ has an antiderivative F. Area is always a nonnegative quantity. The Riemann sum contains terms such as ƒ(ck) ∆xk that give the area of a rectangle when ƒ(ck) is positive. When ƒ(ck) is negative, then the product ƒ(ck) ∆xk is the negative of the rectangle’s area. When we add up such terms for a negative function, we get the negative of the area between the curve and the x-axis. If we then take the absolute value, we obtain the correct positive area.
